bug_semantics: The unauthenticated GET /_instatic/hole/<nodeId> handler treats the attacker-controlled u parameter as the originating page URL and uses its path, slug, and query to render a shared hole, but its process-wide cache key contains only nodeId, publish version, and u's normalized inner query. Because u's pathname is content-varying but absent from the key, an attacker can render route-dependent HTML for a chosen pathname into the slot later used by a legitimate request with the same nodeId, version, and query.
flaw_origin: Commit f066a8838e49ba211250c56c2955a25689e5e7ca first forwarded location.pathname + location.search as u, parsed u into pageUrl, exposed pageUrl-derived route.path and route.slug to rendering and request-dependent loop sources, and simultaneously keyed shared-hole responses as v=<version>&normalizeQuery(pageUrl.searchParams), omitting the content-varying pageUrl pathname. The older hole cache existed, but its parent did not accept u or render from an attacker-selected page URL, so it did not contain this poisoning mechanism.
ai_marker: absent: git cat-file commit f066a8838e49ba211250c56c2955a25689e5e7ca shows human author and committer DavidBabinec <hello@davidbabinec.com>; the complete BIC message has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, AI attribution, or other trailer.
evidence: Advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9p8f-ppfj-8gc5 and NVD CVE-2026-72587 describe unauthenticated shared render-cache poisoning through 0.0.14 via u; GitHub lists both affected and patched versions as Unknown and provides no fix reference. Vulnerable flow: at current main a0b1e4e522b2b5813fa07655d34335309f520c53, server/handlers/cms/hole.ts:217 reads url.searchParams.get('u'), lines 220-226 turn it into pageUrl and route, lines 229 and 252-257 pass its query/path/slug into rendering, while lines 258-262 key getOrRender by nodeId plus v and normalizeQuery(pageUrl.searchParams), not pageUrl.pathname. server/publish/holeRuntime.ts:38-39 sends location.pathname + location.search as u. BIC: git log -L 215,223:server/handlers/cms/hole.ts identifies f066a8838e49ba211250c56c2955a25689e5e7ca as adding the u parse; git log -L 258,262 and git log -S'normalizeQuery(pageUrl.searchParams)' identify the same commit as adding the path-omitting shared key. Direct parent-tree verification: git show 2b1ae37a6716efcf4c208d980433f59af79c47fc:server/handlers/cms/hole.ts shows no u read, pageUrl construction, route frame derived from u, or u-derived request context; it cached the then-non-u-dependent fragment using url.search. Version check: git tag --contains f066a8838e49ba211250c56c2955a25689e5e7ca returns every release v0.0.1 through v0.0.16, including advisory boundary v0.0.14 at 1dbf0f66c5e0f4797d27a91780ea99dabdc48ede. Contrary to the advisory's 'through 0.0.14' wording, v0.0.15 at 68a4b46eb437024c1af07c514f115ecc15d2144a, v0.0.16 at 3af80cc8daa7a6737d2d53801b33ac23f1ee60a5, and current main retain the same key; git diff v0.0.14..v0.0.15 shows no change to hole.ts, holeRuntime.ts, or renderCache.ts. Fix search: the relevant -S history has only the BIC, no later removal/replacement; upstream's latest public main is the same a0b1e4e522b2b5813fa07655d34335309f520c53. Commit-object attribution: git cat-file commit on the BIC supplies the human identities and marker-free message quoted in ai_marker.
reasoning: The original Layer C hole feature cached fragments, but before f066a8838e49ba211250c56c2955a25689e5e7ca the endpoint had no attacker-controlled originating-page URL and did not derive route-sensitive output from u. The BIC made u influence the rendered route path/slug and source request while varying the shared key only by u's query. Two requests whose u values have different pathnames but the same inner query therefore collide; the first unauthenticated request populates the process-wide entry and subsequent legitimate visitors receive its route-dependent body until invalidation or eviction. Both the tainted render input and the incomplete cache key first appear together in this single non-merge commit, so no squash decomposition is needed, and the immediate parent directly proves the mechanism absent. The BIC predates and belongs to every tagged release, satisfying the lower affected boundary, but public history disproves a patch at 0.0.15: later tags and main retain the vulnerable lines, so no real fix SHA can be supplied. Under the BIC-only attribution rule, the human author/committer and complete absence of AI trailers or bot identity require NOT_AI.
remaining_gap: The vulnerability remains unpatched in the available public history through main a0b1e4e522b2b5813fa07655d34335309f520c53 (2026-08-21): there is no fix or direct-fix SHA, and the advisory supplies no patched version or fix reference. Its claim 'through 0.0.14' is inconsistent with unchanged vulnerable code in public v0.0.15 and v0.0.16.
